# Claude Code seats may run docker exec, cp and compose on the plane containers

## Context

The operator asked for the post-merge run of Brain #417 on the local plane today (2026-10-12): a fresh backup, then the merged retirement CLI inside the orchestrator container, dry run and `--apply`. The backup and the dry run ran. The `--apply` invocation was refused twice by the Claude Code auto-mode classifier ("Modify Shared Resources"), as was copying the merged script into the container (`docker cp`), and the seat's attempt to add an allow rule to its own `.claude/settings.local.json` ("Self-Modification"). The operator then authorized updating the local running containers in chat and asked for the rule to arrive through a reviewed PR instead.

Why this never bit before: the recorded container updates (for example Emmy's four-container cut to Brain `6de77a36` on 2026-10-08, Memory Core turn `5362822e`) ran on harnesses that prompt the human per escalated call, and the operator approved each one. Claude Code's auto mode has no prompt; a call the classifier judges destructive is refused outright, and only a permission rule in settings changes that. Operator's chat authorization does not reach the classifier.

## The Problem

Plane maintenance that a seat owns (a scoped Chroma delete under the heavy-maintenance lease, a script copy into a container, a compose recreate at a merged revision) cannot be executed from a Claude Code seat in auto mode, even with the operator's explicit authorization in chat. The remaining routes are the operator running the command by hand or a seat on another harness, both of which split the owner from the executor and the receipt from the lane.

## The Architectural Reality

- The committed, reviewed allow-list is `.claude/settings.template.json`; the file a seat actually loads, `.claude/settings.json`, is gitignored (`.gitignore:124`) and generated from the template by seat provisioning, which adds the seat's hooks (turn presence, harness-id guard, wake arming, lane-state stop) and nothing under `permissions`. On this seat the two permission blocks are byte-identical. `.claude/settings.local.json` is gitignored too (`~/.config/git/ignore`), so neither generated file can carry a reviewed rule; the template can.
- In auto mode an allow rule is honored without consulting the classifier unless `autoMode.classifyAllShell` is set; this repository's `.claude/settings.json` sets `autoMode` prompt customisation only and leaves that flag unset. The refusal message names the remedy: "add a permission rule for Bash to their settings."
- Rule syntax: `Bash(prefix *)` with mid-pattern wildcards, as the existing deny `Bash(git push* --force* origin dev*)` shows.
- The plane's compose project is `neo-local-agent-os`; every container of it carries that prefix (`neo-local-agent-os-orchestrator-1`, `-mc-server-1`, `-kb-server-1`, `-fleet-server-1`, `-chroma-1`, `-ingress-1`).

## The Fix

Add five allow rules to `permissions.allow` in `.claude/settings.template.json`, each binding the container operand: the container name sits immediately after `docker exec` and its fixed flags, and the only `*` is trailing. Everything before the `*` is matched as written, so the rule cannot be satisfied by a container name that appears later in the command (review 5490177767, RA-1):

```json
"Bash(docker exec neo-local-agent-os-orchestrator-1 *)",
"Bash(docker exec -i -w /app neo-local-agent-os-orchestrator-1 *)",
"Bash(docker exec neo-local-agent-os-mc-server-1 *)",
"Bash(docker exec neo-local-agent-os-kb-server-1 *)",
"Bash(docker exec neo-local-agent-os-fleet-server-1 *)"
```

The orchestrator carries the two forms maintenance uses (a plain exec for `backup.mjs`, the stdin form for a merged script); the three app servers carry the plain form. Inside a listed container the seat acts as that container's user, which is the allowance the operator gave; the pre-run backup discipline (#417) is the guard on what runs there. Compound commands are split on shell operators and each part must match a rule on its own, so a trailing `*` grants nothing after `&&`, `;` or `|`.

Each seat's generated `.claude/settings.json` takes the block by explicit copy: the Brain materializer (`ai/scripts/setup/initServerConfigs.mjs`, `initClaudeSettings`) clones the template only when the active file is absent and otherwise ensures the `hooks` block, preserving other keys. A merged template is therefore not a rollout to existing seats; AC-2 names the copy.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.claude/settings.template.json` → `permissions.allow` (copied into each seat's gitignored `.claude/settings.json`) | Claude Code settings (project scope; the template is the reviewed source) | the five rules are honored, without a prompt, for every Claude Code seat whose generated settings carry them, in every permission mode that would otherwise prompt or classify | a seat whose generated file lacks the block keeps prompting (default mode) or classifying (auto mode); other harnesses are unaffected | this ticket | AC-1, AC-2, AC-3 |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — `.claude/settings.template.json` carries the five rules in `permissions.allow`; the file stays valid JSON and every existing allow, deny and ask entry is preserved (`jq` diff of the arrays against `dev` shows five additions and nothing else).
- [ ] **AC-2** — *(post-merge)* From a Claude Code seat in auto mode whose generated `.claude/settings.json` carries the merged template's rules (copied explicitly, since the materializer does not add them to an existing file), `docker exec -i -w /app neo-local-agent-os-orchestrator-1 node --input-type=module - --apply --confirm CONFIRM_RETIRE_LEGACY_CONVERSATION_ROWS < <file>` runs without a classifier refusal; the #417 receipt is the witness.
- [ ] **AC-3** — The boundary holds under the documented matching semantics (`*` matches any text including spaces; everything before the first `*` matched as written; compound commands split on shell operators): a non-executing probe that re-implements those semantics admits the three maintenance commands of 2026-10-12 and rejects every control in the review (an unrelated container with the plane name in its argument, a name-prefix look-alike, an unlisted flag form, `docker cp`, `docker compose -p unrelated …`, `down --volumes` on the plane project, `docker rm`, `docker volume`, and operator-chained deletions). The probe and its output are quoted on the PR; it is evidence about the rules' text, not a run of the harness.

## Out of Scope

Rules for other harnesses (Codex, Gemini, OpenCode keep their own prompts); `docker rm`, `docker volume`, `docker system`, image deletion; changes to `autoMode` prompt customisation; any `.claude/settings.local.json` content. **Deferred, not rejected (review 5490177767):** `docker cp` into a plane container (the stdin route runs a merged script without it, and a cp rule cannot bind the source endpoint) and `docker compose` recreates (a text rule cannot bind the project, the compose files and the operation at once; a recreate allowance arrives with a checked entry-point script the rule can name exactly).

## Avoided Traps

- A blanket `Bash(docker *)`: it would also allow volume and image deletion without a judgment.
- A container name behind a leading `*` (`Bash(docker exec *neo-local-agent-os-*)`, the first head of PR #19650): the `*` matches spaces, so the name may sit in the inner command's argument while the actual container is unrelated. Bind the operand position; keep `*` trailing.
- Putting the rule in the gitignored local file: unreviewable, per-seat, and the seat cannot write it anyway.
- Switching seats to `bypassPermissions`: removes every gate, not one.

```

```

The same invocation had been refused twice at 11:07Z and 11:12Z.
